turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come on through, that chair's fine. How are you going.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): umm not brilliant. Sorry, I was pacing in the corridor, I do that when I'm nervous.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): You're alright. What brought you in today?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I've been so tired. That's why I came. I can hardly get through a day.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tell me what the tiredness is actually like.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Heavy, like my arms are full of sand. umm it started since Diwali or after, I think, or maybe last winter, or the one before. I can't actually date it.
[SEG0007] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She nods off on the tram most nights. I'm her support worker, I tag along when her anxiety's up.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): And stairs. Two flights at the flat and I'm breathless, properly puffed. On the flat I'm okay.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mainly the stairs, or other times too?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Mainly the stairs. And I've been craving ice. I chew it straight from the freezer, heaps, every night.
[SEG0011] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Mm. The ice tray's bare every morning.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about your periods, heavy or all over the shop?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. They're normal. Same as always, not heavy, pretty regular.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it my heart though? Am I going to collapse on the stairs? I can't stop thinking about it.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): I get why that's frightening. Nothing you've said so far sounds like a heart attack, and you're comfy sitting there. We'll still check you properly.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): What about cancer then. Tired means cancer on the internet.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's a horrible worry, and it's not the first thing this story makes me think of. Anyone in the family with long term problems, blood issues, that kind of thing?

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): um my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, my other sister has pressure but no sugar, and my older sister's fine as far as I know. No one with cancer that I've heard of.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): What's ordinary life like for you, work and food and the rest?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I work at the council library, about twenty, well actually about thirty hours a week, sometimes a bit over if someone's sick. Strict vegetarian, no meat no fish no eggs even, have been since uni. Exercise is basically none, I used to walk to the tram and I don't anymore. Alcohol is one glass of wine on a Friday if that, not through the week.
[SEG0021] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She does her own food, same lentils most days. I don't shop for her.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you on any tablets from the chemist just now?

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I was on ferrous sulphaite, uh 200 milligrams once a day, for low iron. I stopped it in March, it wrecked my stomach. They wrote me B12 tablets at the uni clinic too but I never took them, not even once.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. So the B12 never got started. Did the iron do anything before you stopped?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): err maybe a tiny bit, I don't know. I only lasted a few weeks. Was it stupid to stop?
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not stupid, just good you told me. Quick look, the inside of your lower lids is a bit pale. Pulse is 88 beats a minute, and your blood pressure is 112 over 74.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Pale, is that bad? Am I already anaemic? Do people get a transfusion for this?

[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pale lids can fit with low iron, but looking isn't the same as a result, and nothing here says transfusion. My working thought is this may be iron deficiency, with the tiredness, the ice and the vegetarian food, but that's provisional until the numbers are back.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): So what tests are you doing? Is it heaps of needles, because I really hate needles.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Just one draw. I'll book a full blood count, iron studies, B12 and folate now, for the tiredness and the ice craving. They can take it after we're done.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I have to stop being vegetarian? I won't eat meat. And if the tests come back normal, then what happens?

[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): You don't have to eat meat. Add lentils, tofu and leafy greens, and have orange or capsicum with them so the iron absorbs better. Hold off restarting the ferrous sulphaite until we see those results.
[SEG0033] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I can nudge her about the greens. She goes blank when she's anxious.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): What if the stairs get worse before the results. Like I properly can't breathe.

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you can't catch your breath at rest, or you get chest pain, don't wait, come straight in or go to emergency. Otherwise I'll see you back in a fortnight with the results.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): A fortnight. Okay. You reckon it's not my heart?
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): I don't think it's your heart from what you've told me. The bloods will tell us much more than I can today, and we'll go through them together.

spec.situation: Tired young woman, strict vegetarian, breathless on stairs, craving ice; periods normal by her account; blood tests planned; diet advice.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

omissions.text: Patient reported the tiredness feels 'heavy, like my arms are full of sand.'
Caregiver reported the patient nods off on the tram most nights.
Patient said periods are 'same as always' as well as not heavy and pretty regular.
Family history also included mother without diabetes, older sister well, and no known family history of cancer.
Patient follows a vegan diet in practice: strict vegetarian with no meat, fish, or eggs.
Patient had stopped ferrous sulfate in March because it 'wrecked my stomach' (stomach upset/intolerance).
Patient was prescribed B12 tablets previously at the university clinic but never started them, not even once.
Doctor advised that one blood draw would be needed and that it could be taken after the consultation.
Doctor reassured that the story so far did not sound like a heart attack and later said they did not think it was the patient's heart based on the history.
